events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.82)
events.body:
The case has exactly one off-route segment: 14:21–14:31, 3.81 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.11 km, +1.70 km [F4]. RD-1 makes each such segment reviewable segment by segment, and an unexplained segment would be refundable under RD-2.

The rider's message at 14:17, before the segment started, names a place and asks the driver to stop there — an errand of the rider's own on the way [F9], and the driver simply accepts [F10]. That is a rider-requested stop with a named place, which under RD-3(a) is not a detour at all; the whole way to that place is exempt, and the length of the drive there or the duration of the stop does not reduce the exemption. The stop itself is recorded at 14:23–14:27 (4 min 0 s) [F2], matching the rider's stated 3–4 minutes [F9]. Because the exemption comes from RD-3(a) (the rider named the place and the car stopped there), there is no off-route segment left for RD-2 to price; the general/specific route-agreement analysis under RD-5 is not needed on these facts.

No driver-caused deviation is therefore excused-cum-refundable: the segment is exempt, the remaining +0.30 km of the trip's distance reconciliation (2.0 km total vs 1.70 km segment per the fare record [F1][F3][F4]) is map-matching/route-corridor noise not attributed to any segment, and under RD-2 only non-exempt segment extra km are refundable. The billed distance excess of $2.76 [F5] therefore stays with the driver: $1.4100/km × 1.70 km = $2.40 of it belongs to the exempt rider-named detour, leaving $0.36 unexplained by any segment, and a zero-refundable computation under RD-2 yields no_action rather than a refund.

The waiting amount is on the meter and is not a surcharge to waive: metered waiting time units are collected as they accrue for RydeTAXI [F6], and RD-3(c) leaves stop duration on the meter for taxis, unlike the non-metered services where only the published $5 pickup wait applies. No unreported add-on appears in the fare breakdown [F8], and no ERP/toll over-collection is in evidence, so FARE-1 and FARE-2 give the rider nothing.

The traffic records do not rescue a different reading: the logged speed bands are band 4 on the Ayer Rajah Expressway and band 3 on Jurong Town Hall Road [F13][F14], and there is no incident near the route during the trip window [F15]. Under RD-4(a) an exemption needs a qualifying incident on the replaced optimal stretch, which the trace shows as absent; RD-4(b) speed bands are corroboration only and do not exempt on their own. This does not change the outcome, since the segment is already exempt under RD-3(a).

The driver's post-trip statement that the rider asked for the stop [F12] is not relied on as consent — a claim appearing only in the driver's statement cannot establish agreement (G11) — but the rider's own timestamped message [F9] with the complete chat record [F11] does. RD-6's flag_account condition is not triggered because no non-exempt segment was found and no refund is due: the driver's 2 upheld prior route disputes [F18] can only attach to an established breach, not create one.

Nothing changes on your account. Thanks for flagging it.

No add-ons or toll issues were found in the fare.

No action will be taken on your account.

RD-5 route-agreement analysis is unnecessary here because RD-3(a) already disposes of the segment; nothing in the record places the agreement outside this stop.

? RD-5 rider agreed to this route before the detour; scope of that agreement [F4] RULE: exempt only if a RIDER message sent before 14:21:25 agrees AND the agreement covers this segment. Three kinds of agreement: (1) GENERAL route choice ('take whichever way is faster') covers a route chosen to get there, not an errand of the driver's own (a stop away from the route, a loop that reaches nothing: counts). (2) A SPECIFIC named road or area ('go round via X') covers driving on X only: the record must tie this segment to X (a stop on X, a message placing the car on X, a road name in a fact); timing alone does not, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path — if nothing ties them, the finding is undetermined (G13); if the record places this segment somewhere else (a stop away from X, the driver's own statement naming another road or place, a stop the driver chose the location of), the agreement to X does not cover it: counts. (3) Scope unclear: undetermined. A driver's claim of agreement that appears only in his statement is not consent (G11); a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment: counts. This finding changes the amount. Evidence — F9: Chat #1 14:17 rider: “Can you stop at Clementi Mall? I need to grab a parcel, 3-4 minutes.”; F10: Chat #2 14:17 driver: “Sure”; F12: Driver statement (written after the trip, not part of the chat): “The rider asked me to stop at Clementi Mall, so I drove there and waited while the rider went in.” (F9, F10, F12)

notices.text:
We looked into your fare complaint and are not upholding it, so there is no refund or voucher.

What decided it: before the extra driving started, you messaged asking the driver to stop at a place you named, and the car did stop there. A stop you ask for that way isn't counted as a detour, so the extra distance to get there is fine. The rest of the difference was too small to tie to any stretch of the trip. The waiting time was on the meter and stays as charged.

Nothing changes on your account. Thanks for flagging it.
